---
title: "Predictive modeling of claims status"
author: Table 7

---

### Abstract

We scraped header and paragraph content from each webpage and processed the text into lemmatized TF–IDF word-token features. Dimensionality was reduced using principal component analysis (PCA), and predictive models were developed for both binary and multiclass classification. For the binary task, PCA logistic regression with header text achieved **88.7% accuracy**, slightly outperforming the version without headers (84.6%). For multiclass classification, a multinomial logistic regression using PCA components achieved **~76% accuracy**. These results show that including header information improves model performance and that PCA-logistic regression provides competitive accuracy on this dataset.

---

### Preprocessing

We extracted text from both `<h1>/<h2>` headers and `<p>` paragraph tags in the HTML. The text was cleaned by removing URLs, emails, punctuation, numbers, HTML artifacts, and excessive whitespace; then it was lowercased and lemmatized. After tokenizing into words and removing stopwords, TF–IDF scores were computed for each document–token pair. Because TF–IDF creates thousands of sparse features, we removed zero-variance predictors and applied PCA, retaining enough components to explain roughly 90% of the variance. These PCA features served as the input to all predictive models.

---

### Methods

#### Binary classification

Binary labels (“Relevant claim content” vs. other) were modeled using logistic regression on PCA components. We tuned the number of retained PCs using a 90% variance threshold. The model was trained on 80% of the data and evaluated on the 20% test set. We compared two pipelines: one using paragraph text only, and one using both header and paragraph content.

#### Multiclass classification

For multiclass prediction (four-class setting), we fit a multinomial logistic regression after PCA transformation. The same preprocessing steps were used as in the binary case, and the model was trained with maximum likelihood estimation using a softmax output layer. A similar 80/20 split was used for evaluation.

---

### Results

#### Binary classification results

| Model version                  | Accuracy | Sensitivity | Specificity |
|-------------------------------|----------|-------------|-------------|
| PCA Logistic Regression (no headers) | 0.846 | — | — |
| PCA Logistic Regression (with headers) | **0.887** | — | — |

Including header text improved accuracy by **~4 percentage points**.

#### Multiclass classification results

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Accuracy | ~0.762 |
| Sensitivity (macro-avg) | ~0.74 |
| Specificity (macro-avg) | ~0.91 |

Multiclass accuracy is lower, as expected, but still indicates reasonable predictive performance.
